extracted.intended_audience: organizations and practitioners that publish nonpartisan fact-checks (fact-checking organizations, editors, and fact-checkers)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of organizational commitments and standards for groups that regularly publish nonpartisan fact-checks of statements by public figures, institutions, and widely circulated claims. The page specifies commitments on nonpartisanship, source and funding transparency, methodology, corrections, and use of the IFCN badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: A commitment to Nonpartisanship and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations fact-check claims using the same standard for every fact check. They do not concentrate their fact-checking on any one side. They follow the same process for every fact check and let the evidence dictate the conclusions. Signatories do not advocate or take policy positions on the issues they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply identical standards and processes across subjects and political actors; avoid advocacy or policy positions; do not target only one side or group. The emphasis is on evidence-led conclusions and consistent treatment across fact checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: A commitment to Transparency of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories want their readers to be able to verify findings themselves. Signatories provide all sources in enough detail that readers can replicate their work, except in cases where a source’s personal security could be compromised. In such cases, signatories provide as much detail as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish full sourcing and documentation for verification and replication. When source safety is a concern, redact identifying details only as necessary and explain limitations to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: A commitment to Transparency of Funding & Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations are transparent about their funding sources. If they accept funding from other organizations, they ensure that funders have no influence over the conclusions the fact-checkers reach in their reports. Signatory organizations detail the professional background of all key figures in the organization and explain the organizational structure and legal status. Signatories clearly indicate a way for readers to communicate with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly disclose funders and organizational/legal structure; document key staff backgrounds; ensure and demonstrate firewalls so funders cannot influence findings; provide clear contact channels for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: A commitment to Transparency of Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories explain the methodology they use to select, research, write, edit, publish and correct their fact checks. They encourage readers to send claims to fact-check and are transparent on why and how they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe selection criteria for claims, research and editorial workflows, fact-checking methods, and publishing/correction practices. Make submission mechanisms and rationale for choosing claims visible to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: A commitment to an Open & Honest Corrections Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories publish their corrections policy and follow it scrupulously. They correct clearly and transparently in line with the corrections policy, seeking so far as possible to ensure that readers see the corrected version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and publish a clear corrections policy; correct errors promptly and visibly; ensure corrected versions are made available and that readers are made aware of corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFCN badge usage and signatory listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations that have obtained IFCN verification are encouraged to publish a badge in their homepage, however, the complete list of signatories is here. Any other organization that holds the IFCN badge and is not listed is NOT a signatory to the code of principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display IFCN verification badge if verified, but readers should consult the official signatory list for authoritative membership; the badge alone does not substitute for being listed as a signatory. Do not claim signatory status if not listed.
